scope: Different-author, static-only hammer review of the exact M1900 clean-environment two-axis C2 fast-min hold-repair runner. The review rechecked the M1897 five P1 corrections, exact upstream identities and seals, two-axis/two-DC cardinality, per-axis 5 percent area ceilings, 0.070-to-0.050 ns hold contract, setup/hold/DRC gates, attempt-before-license semantics, failure terminal behavior, publication proof and raw claim boundary. It also performed in-memory semantic-authority and safe standalone bash signal-trap attacks. It performed no license query, attempt creation, Design Compiler, PrimeTime, Formality, VCS, PTPX, result publication, runner/Tcl/predecessor mutation or docs/359 mutation.
verdict: FAIL CLOSED. M1900 materially repairs all five M1897 engineering defects in the ordinary non-signal path: clean absolute tool execution, attempt staging and publication before license, a terminal quarantine on normal nonzero exits, five-section zero-violation DRC gating, and post-publication source-absence plus destination double-seal proof. The frozen two-axis inputs, exact 5 percent per-axis area caps, fixed two-call loop, 3.000/0.200 ns timing contract, 0.070 ns optimization then 0.050 ns reporting contract, setup/hold gates and raw no-PT/no-Formality/no-power claim boundary are also preserved. Launch remains forbidden because all four authority digests are caller-controlled positional self-pins and the semantic parser accepts an entirely caller-forged minimal review/release/audit triplet; additionally, the shared signal/EXIT trap can observe rc=0 on SIGTERM at a builtin boundary and leave a consumed attempt without RESULT or FAILURE. No M1902 release, M1900 license query, attempt or DC is authorized.

findings.finding: Runner, review, release and audit digests are all caller-controlled positional self-pins; there is no independent launch root.
findings.evidence: Lines 6-8 receive all four digests from argv. Lines 70-90 compare canonical files to those same caller values. An in-memory reproduction of the exact assertions accepted an entirely caller-created minimal M1901 object, exact-shape M1902 object and minimal M1903 object; M1901 and M1903 required no schema at all. A modified runner can likewise be passed its own modified SHA together with matching forged authority objects.
findings.impact: The exact reviewed runner and independently released authority are not fail-closed. A mutually consistent caller-selected chain can authorize a source that was never the M1901-reviewed source, repeating the core self-pin defect from M1897 with positional arguments instead of environment variables.
findings.required_fix: Consume an external launch root that is not supplied by this invocation. Freeze the exact runner/review/release/audit tuple in a zero-argument, independently reviewed authority/launcher and publish one exact launch command; do not accept those SHA values from argv or environment. Also require exact review/audit schema, milestone, reviewer separation and full identity semantics.

findings.finding: The shared EXIT/INT/TERM/HUP handler can treat a real signal as rc=0 and omit the required terminal quarantine after attempt consumption.
findings.evidence: Lines 48-57 use one finish function whose failure branch is conditional on entry $?. A safe standalone reproduction with the same trap structure delivered SIGTERM during a bash builtin loop and observed rc=0. In that case finish clears all traps and exits zero without lines 50-53. The M1900 runner has multiple shell-builtin/loop regions after line 109 publishes ATTEMPT, so the same state can leave canonical ATTEMPT plus unsealed WORK but no RESULT or FAILURE.
findings.impact: A consumed one-shot attempt can lack an auditable terminal state and the process can exit zero on interruption, violating partial-attempt terminality and fail-closed no-retry semantics.
findings.required_fix: Use distinct signal traps that call an idempotent handler with forced nonzero codes (for example INT=130, TERM=143, HUP=129), and an EXIT trap that passes the real command status explicitly. Every signal after ACTIVE becomes one must seal and publish the fixed failure quarantine before nonzero exit.

findings.finding: The future M1901 and M1903 semantic checks omit schema, milestone, reviewer separation and most review authorization identity fields.
findings.evidence: Lines 79-81 check only status, counts and runner SHA for M1901. Lines 88-90 check only status, counts and a three-field identity for M1903. The synthetic objects that passed these checks had no schema or reviewer_identity.
findings.impact: Minimal fabricated objects can look equivalent to complete independent reviews, which amplifies P1-01 and weakens later auditability.
findings.required_fix: Require exact schema/milestone, fixed different reviewer identities, complete upstream identity tuples and authorization limits for both reviews, in addition to valid double seals.
